acme_fintech_julia: Hey, hitting a customer bug — streaming tool-call args are getting truncated mid-JSON when we call the payments tool. Customer sees schema validation errors and failed payouts.

support-ops: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the raw chunk you observed and error from the API? Any repro steps?

acme_fintech_julia: Here is the chunk we captured from the stream (we see this in our proxy logs right before the tool invocation fails):
```json
{"action":"run_payment","args":{"amount":125.00,"currency":"USD","recipient":{"name":"ACME Corp","acc
```
That truncated "account" key; runtime throws a schema validation: `400_toolcall_arg_incomplete` and the tool never runs. TraceID: trace_0a1b2c3d

maya: Oof. Are you using the hosted API or Dedicated? Which SDK version / streaming mode (SSE vs chunked HTTP) are you using?

acme_fintech_julia: Hosted API. Using our internal streaming client which opens an HTTP POST with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and writes partial JSON as events arrive. SDK is not involved. Repro is easy: send a large tool arg so the server stream splits in the middle of a string.

cory: Quick thought — we expect tool-call args to be delivered as complete JSON objects to the runtime layer. If the proxy or client splits a JSON token across TCP chunks and our stream assembler passes pieces directly into the JSON parser without message boundaries, you can get a JSONDecodeError. Do we have the exact runtime exception from the logs?

sre-bot: automated: runtime/ingest error: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 85 (char 84)
stack: runtime/parser.py:142 -> runtime/handler.py:78
metadata: commit=rel/2026.02.1 node=host-12 region=us-west1 trace=trace_0a1b2c3d

maya: Thanks @sre-bot. @cory, any known regressions around streaming reassembly?

cory: Not a regression but an edge-case: our streaming ingestion expects each SSE/data event to contain a complete JSON payload for tool calls. When clients use raw chunked HTTP writes, some front proxies (ingress-nginx, old HTTP proxies) will split in the middle of a token. Our current assembler concatenates chunks but tries to parse each buffer opportunistically which can hit partial parse attempts. Two immediate mitigations:
- Client-side: buffer until you have a full JSON object (or ensure each tool-call is sent in one chunk / one SSE event).
- Ingress-side: disable proxy_buffering and ensure `proxy_request_buffering off;` (nginx) so we get passthrough streams that preserve event boundaries.

ingrid: For customers who can't change clients, we can also add server-side tolerant reassembly that defers parse until newline or SSE event boundary — but that needs eng-runtime work and QA.

acme_fintech_julia: Customer is on a managed integration; they cannot easily change their client. Can you document a reproducible curl command so we can show them cause?

cory: Sure — minimal repro using chunked transfer: 
```
printf '{"action":"run_payment","args":{"amount":125.00,"currency":"USD","recipient":{"name":"ACME Corp","account":"123' > part1.json
printf '456789","bank":"X"}}}' > part2.json
(echo -n; cat part1.json; sleep 0.2; cat part2.json) | \
  curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream?model=tool-runner" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
    --data-binary @- 
```
This will show the server receiving a split token and reproducing the JSONDecodeError.

support-ops: Does this only affect tool calls or also normal chat message streaming?

cory: Mostly tool-call args payloads because they contain nested JSON that we hand off directly to the schema validator. Chat text streaming is mostly tolerant because we treat chunks as text continuations. Tool args are parsed into structured objects as soon as we detect a call, so partial parses fail fast.

maya: OK. Next steps? Customer needs an immediate workaround and we need a long-term fix.

cory: For immediate: ask the customer to enable SSE framing or stop using raw chunked writes so each tool-call payload lands as one event. If they can't, we can configure the customer routing to go through an ingress that doesn't split (set `proxy_buffering off`). For long-term: eng-runtime will add reassembly that waits for closing brace or SSE event boundary before parsing and adds safer incremental parse logic. I can own the RFC and a patch.

ingrid: I'll capture the repro in an internal runbook and add a note: "If you see `400_toolcall_arg_incomplete` for tool-runner, check Transfer-Encoding and proxy buffer settings."

acme_fintech_julia: That works. I've informed the customer of the workaround and gave them the curl repro. They will try to disable their proxy buffering and report back. Thanks.

support-ops: Escalating to eng-runtime: assigned to cory, priority P2 for now (impacting payouts). Customer case updated with repro, logs, and suggested mitigations. :white_check_mark:

cory: I'll open an internal PR and add a feature flag to enable tolerant reassembly for affected accounts so we can roll out safely. Will post updates here.

support-ops: Closing thread for now; will reopen if customer reports failures after trying workaround."
